Name: Dumbbell bench press
Description: A free-weight press that trains the chest, with help from the shoulders and triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand and your feet flat on the floor.
1. Start with the dumbbells beside the chest and the wrists stacked over the elbows.
2. Press the weights up until the arms are extended without snapping the elbows locked.
3. Lower the dumbbells with control until the upper arms are near the sides of the chest.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Bouncing the weights off the chest, letting the elbows flare straight out, or lifting the hips to finish the press.

Name: Barbell bench press
Description: A flat barbell press for the middle of the chest, with the triceps helping.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on a flat bench with the feet on the floor. Grip the bar just outside the shoulders and hold it over the chest.
1. Lower the bar to the middle of the chest.
2. Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
3. Press the bar up until the arms are extended without snapping the elbows locked.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest, flaring the elbows straight out, or lifting the hips off the bench.

Name: Incline barbell press
Description: An incline barbell press for the upper chest, with the shoulders and triceps helping.
Instructions:
Setup: Set a bench to a modest incline, plant the feet, and hold the bar over the upper chest with the hands just outside the shoulders.
1. Lower the bar toward the upper chest.
2. Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
3. Press the bar up until the arms are extended without locking them hard.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Setting the bench nearly upright so the shoulders take over, or bouncing the bar off the chest.

Name: Decline barbell press
Description: A decline barbell press for the lower chest, with the triceps helping.
Instructions:
Setup: Secure the feet on a decline bench and lie back with the bar over the lower chest. Grip it just outside the shoulders.
1. Lower the bar toward the lower chest.
2. Keep both feet secured so the body does not slide.
3. Press the bar up until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Using a steep decline that strains the head, or letting the bar drift toward the face.

Name: Bench dumbbell press
Description: A beginner press on a flat bench, with a shorter range than a full dumbbell bench press.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on a flat bench with the feet on the floor and a light dumbbell in each hand beside the chest.
1. Press the dumbbells up until the arms are extended.
2. Lower only as far as the shoulders stay comfortable.
3. Keep the wrists above the elbows.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Dropping the elbows below the bench, or lifting the hips to finish the press.

Name: Bench hex press
Description: A press on a flat bench with the dumbbells kept together over the chest.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on a flat bench with the feet on the floor and the dumbbells pressed together over the chest.
1. Press the dumbbells up while keeping them touching.
2. Lower until the upper arms are near the bench.
3. Keep squeezing the dumbbells toward each other.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Letting the dumbbells drift apart, or bouncing them off the chest.

Name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
Description: A row with the chest braced on an incline bench so the back does the pull.
Instructions:
Setup: Set a bench to a modest incline and lie chest-down with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging.
1. Pull the dumbbells toward the hips.
2. Squeeze the shoulder blades together.
3. Lower until the arms are long.
Breathing: Exhale as you pull. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench to swing the weights, or shrugging the shoulders.

Name: Incline chest-supported reverse fly
Description: A reverse fly with the chest on an incline bench for the rear of the shoulders.
Instructions:
Setup: Set a bench to a modest incline and lie chest-down with a light dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging.
1. Keep a small bend in the elbows.
2. Raise the arms out to the sides until they are about level with the back.
3. Lower the dumbbells with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you raise. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench, or shrugging to finish the raise.

Name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
Description: An overhead press seated on a bench with the back supported.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit on a bench with a back support, feet flat, and a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
1. Press the dumbbells overhead until the arms are extended.
2. Keep the ribs against the back support.
3. Lower the weights to shoulder height with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Arching off the back support, or bouncing out of the bottom.

Name: Bench overhead dumbbell extension
Description: A seated overhead extension on a bench for the long head of the triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit on a bench with the back supported and hold one dumbbell overhead in both hands. Keep the ribs down.
1. Bend the elbows and lower the dumbbell behind the head.
2. Keep the upper arms close to the ears.
3. Straighten the elbows to return the weight overhead.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide, or dropping the weight onto the neck.

Name: Chest-supported dumbbell kickback
Description: A triceps kickback with the chest braced on a bench.
Instructions:
Setup: Kneel or hinge with the chest supported on a bench. Hold a light dumbbell with the upper arm beside the ribs.
1. Keep the upper arm still.
2. Straighten the elbow until the forearm points back.
3. Bend the elbow to return the dumbbell.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Swinging the upper arm, or lifting the chest off the bench.

Name: Bench close-grip dumbbell press
Description: A narrow dumbbell press on a flat bench for the medial head of the triceps, with the chest assisting.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on a flat bench with the dumbbells touching over the chest and the elbows close to the sides.
1. Press until the arms are straight.
2. Lower until the upper arms are near the bench.
3. Keep the elbows pointing down, not out.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Flaring the elbows, or bouncing the dumbbells off the chest.

Name: Dumbbell fly
Description: An open-arm chest movement that keeps a soft bend in the elbows.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on a bench with the dumbbells above the chest and a slight bend in the elbows.
1. Open the arms in a wide arc until you feel a comfortable stretch across the chest.
2. Keep the elbow bend steady rather than turning the movement into a press.
3. Bring the dumbbells back together over the chest along the same arc.
Breathing: Inhale as the arms open. Exhale as they come together.
Common mistakes: Straightening the arms, dropping the weights too low, or using a load that pulls the shoulders forward.

Name: Push-up
Description: A bodyweight press for the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Place your hands slightly wider than the shoulders and set the body in a straight line from head to heels. Drop to the knees if a full push-up is too hard.
1. Bend the elbows and lower the chest toward the floor.
2. Keep the ribs down and the neck in line with the spine.
3. Press the floor away until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Inhale on the way down. Exhale as you press up.
Common mistakes: Letting the hips sag, shrugging the shoulders toward the ears, or only bending the elbows a few degrees.

Name: Chest press
Description: A machine press that guides the path while the chest and triceps do the work.
Instructions:
Setup: Adjust the seat so the handles sit about chest height. Place your feet on the floor and your back against the pad.
1. Grip the handles and press them forward until the arms are extended.
2. Keep the shoulders down instead of letting them roll toward the ears.
3. Return the handles with control until the elbows are near the torso.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Locking the elbows hard, lifting the hips, or choosing a seat height that makes the shoulders shrug.

Name: Pec deck
Description: A machine fly that brings the arms together in front of the chest.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit with the pads or handles at chest height and your back supported.
1. Open the arms to a comfortable width without forcing a deep stretch.
2. Bring the arms together in front of the chest while the torso stays still.
3. Pause briefly, then return along the same path.
Breathing: Exhale as the arms come together. Inhale as they open.
Common mistakes: Shrugging, leaning forward to finish the rep, or letting the machine pull the shoulders behind the torso.

Name: Dumbbell row
Description: A one-arm free-weight row for the back, with the biceps assisting.
Instructions:
Setup: Support one hand and the same-side knee on a bench. Hold a dumbbell in the free hand with the arm hanging.
1. Keep the back roughly flat and the shoulders square to the floor.
2. Pull the dumbbell toward the hip, leading with the elbow.
3. Lower the weight until the arm is straight again.
Breathing: Exhale as you pull. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Twisting the torso to swing the weight, or shrugging the shoulder instead of pulling with the back.

Name: Barbell row
Description: A two-arm free-weight row that trains the back and biceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Hinge at the hips until the torso is near a comfortable forward angle. Hold the bar with the arms hanging and the knees soft.
1. Brace the trunk so the back does not round as the bar moves.
2. Pull the bar toward the lower ribs or upper abdomen.
3. Lower the bar with control until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you pull. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Jerking with the lower back, standing upright to turn the row into a shrug, or bouncing the bar off the thighs.

Name: Lat pulldown
Description: A machine pull that trains the back and biceps from overhead.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit with the thighs secured and grip the bar a little wider than the shoulders.
1. Start with the arms extended and the shoulders relaxed down.
2. Pull the bar toward the upper chest while the chest stays tall.
3. Return the bar overhead with control until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you pull. Inhale as the bar rises.
Common mistakes: Leaning far back to yank the bar, pulling behind the neck, or only bending the wrists.

Name: Seated cable row
Description: A seated cable pull for the back and biceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit tall with the feet braced and a soft bend in the knees. Hold the handle with the arms extended.
1. Pull the handle toward the abdomen, drawing the elbows back.
2. Keep the chest up and the ribs from flaring.
3. Let the arms straighten again without rounding the back.
Breathing: Exhale as you pull. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Swinging the torso back and forth, or shrugging the shoulders to the ears at the end of the pull.

Name: Dumbbell shoulder press
Description: An overhead free-weight press for the shoulders and triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit or stand with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height and the ribs stacked over the pelvis.
1. Press the dumbbells overhead until the arms are extended.
2. Keep the path slightly in front of the face if straight overhead feels uncomfortable.
3. Lower the weights to shoulder height with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Overarching the lower back, pressing the weights together in a way that shrugs the neck, or bouncing out of the bottom.

Name: Lateral raise
Description: A dumbbell raise that lifts the arms out to the sides.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand with a light dumbbell in each hand and a soft bend in the elbows.
1. Raise the arms out to the sides until they are about shoulder height.
2. Keep the shoulders down and the torso still.
3. Lower the dumbbells with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the weights, shrugging, or turning the movement into a full overhead press.

Name: Shoulder press machine
Description: A guided overhead press for the shoulders and triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Adjust the seat so the handles start near shoulder height.
1. Press the handles up until the arms are extended.
2. Keep the back against the pad and the feet on the floor.
3. Lower the handles to the start without letting the stack crash.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Shrugging at the top, lifting the hips, or using a range that pinches the shoulders.

Name: Lateral raise machine
Description: A machine raise that moves the upper arms out to the sides.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit with the pads against the upper arms and the elbows softly bent.
1. Lift the arms out to about shoulder height.
2. Keep the neck long and the torso against the seat.
3. Lower the pads with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders or leaning to one side to finish the rep.

Name: Dumbbell curl
Description: A standing or seated curl that bends the elbows against dumbbells.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at the sides, and palms facing forward.
1. Curl the dumbbells toward the shoulders without swinging the torso.
2. Keep the elbows close to the ribs.
3. Lower the weights until the arms are nearly straight.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Leaning back, swinging the hips, or letting the elbows drift far forward.

Name: Hammer curl
Description: A neutral-grip dumbbell curl for the biceps and forearms.
Instructions:
Setup: Hold the dumbbells with the palms facing each other and the arms at the sides.
1. Curl the weights toward the shoulders while the palms stay facing in.
2. Keep the elbows beside the torso.
3. Lower the dumbbells under control.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Turning the wrists into a standard curl, or using momentum from the back.

Name: Biceps curl machine
Description: A supported machine curl for the biceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Adjust the seat so the elbows rest on the pad and line up with the machine pivot.
1. Curl the handles toward the shoulders.
2. Keep the elbows on the pad.
3. Lower the handles until the arms are almost straight.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad or cutting the range short so the arms barely move.

Name: Cable curl
Description: A cable curl that keeps tension on the biceps through the rep.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand facing a low cable with a handle or bar in the hands and the elbows at the sides.
1. Curl the handle toward the shoulders without leaning back.
2. Keep the elbows still.
3. Lower the handle until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Letting the cable pull the shoulders forward, or swinging the trunk to start the curl.

Name: Dumbbell overhead extension
Description: An overhead dumbbell movement that straightens the elbows.
Instructions:
Setup: Hold one dumbbell with both hands overhead, or one dumbbell in one hand. Keep the ribs down.
1. Bend the elbows and lower the dumbbell behind the head.
2. Keep the upper arms close to the ears.
3. Straighten the elbows to return the weight overhead.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide, arching the lower back, or dropping the weight onto the neck.

Name: Close-grip barbell press
Description: A narrower barbell press that emphasizes the triceps, with the chest assisting.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on a bench and grip the bar about shoulder-width apart. Keep the feet on the floor.
1. Lower the bar toward the lower chest or upper abdomen with the elbows close to the sides.
2. Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
3. Press the bar up until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Using a grip so narrow that the wrists bend, or bouncing the bar off the chest.

Name: Cable pushdown
Description: A cable extension that straightens the elbows against a high pulley.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand facing a high cable with the elbows bent and held beside the ribs.
1. Straighten the elbows and push the handle toward the thighs.
2. Keep the upper arms still.
3. Let the forearms return until the elbows are bent again.
Breathing: Exhale as you push down. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Letting the elbows drift forward, leaning over the handle, or bending the wrists to move the weight.

Name: Triceps extension machine
Description: A seated machine that trains elbow extension.
Instructions:
Setup: Adjust the seat so the elbows line up with the pivot and the hands rest on the handles.
1. Straighten the elbows against the handles.
2. Keep the back supported.
3. Return until the elbows are bent, without letting the stack slam.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Lifting the shoulders or using a seat height that forces the wrists to bend.

Name: Goblet squat
Description: A dumbbell squat held at the chest for the quadriceps and glutes.
Instructions:
Setup: Hold one dumbbell close to the chest. Stand with the feet about hip to shoulder width and the toes slightly out.
1. Sit the hips down and back while the chest stays tall.
2. Keep the heels down and the knees tracking over the toes.
3. Stand back up by pushing the floor away.
Breathing: Inhale as you descend. Exhale as you stand.
Common mistakes: Letting the heels lift, collapsing the chest, or letting the knees cave inward.

Name: Dumbbell split squat
Description: A split-stance squat with dumbbells for the quadriceps and glutes.
Instructions:
Setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Step one foot back and balance on the ball of the back foot.
1. Lower the back knee toward the floor while the front knee tracks over the foot.
2. Keep the torso upright.
3. Push through the front foot to stand.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you stand.
Common mistakes: Letting the front knee collapse inward, or bouncing the back knee off the floor.

Name: Bodyweight squat
Description: A squat using only body weight for the quadriceps and glutes.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand with the feet about shoulder width and the arms reaching forward for balance if needed.
1. Sit the hips down while the chest stays up.
2. Go as low as you can while the heels stay down and the knees track over the toes.
3. Stand back up and squeeze the glutes at the top without leaning back.
Breathing: Inhale as you sit down. Exhale as you stand.
Common mistakes: Rising onto the toes, rounding the back, or stopping after a very small knee bend.

Name: Leg extension
Description: A machine movement that straightens the knees.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit with the back supported and the pad against the lower shins. Line the knees up with the machine pivot.
1. Straighten the knees to lift the pad.
2. Pause briefly without snapping the knees backward.
3. Lower the pad with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Using momentum, lifting the hips off the seat, or forcing a painful lockout.

Name: Leg press
Description: A machine press for the quadriceps and glutes.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit in the machine with the feet about shoulder width on the platform and the back against the pad.
1. Lower the platform by bending the knees to a comfortable depth.
2. Keep the heels on the platform and the knees tracking over the toes.
3. Press the platform away without locking the knees hard.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Letting the lower back peel off the pad, or bouncing at the bottom.

Name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
Description: A hip hinge with dumbbells for the hamstrings and glutes.
Instructions:
Setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs. Stand with a soft bend in the knees.
1. Push the hips back and lower the dumbbells along the legs.
2. Stop when the hamstrings feel a strong stretch or the back wants to round.
3. Drive the hips forward to stand tall.
Breathing: Inhale as you hinge. Exhale as you stand.
Common mistakes: Squatting the weight down, rounding the back, or yanking the dumbbells with the arms.

Name: Seated leg curl
Description: A machine curl that bends the knees against the hamstrings.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit with the back supported and the leg pad just above the heels. Adjust the thigh pad if the machine has one.
1. Bend the knees and pull the pad downward or backward, following the machine path.
2. Keep the hips still.
3. Return until the knees are nearly straight.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Lifting the hips, swinging the pad, or cutting the movement so the knees barely bend.

Name: Dumbbell hip thrust
Description: A hip extension with a dumbbell across the hips that loads the lower and middle gluteus maximus.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit on the floor with the upper back against a bench and a dumbbell across the hips. Bend the knees and place the feet flat.
1. Drive through the heels and lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
2. Squeeze the lower and middle gluteus maximus, and keep the ribs down rather than arching the lower back.
3. Lower the hips with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Pushing through the toes only, overextending the lower back, or letting the dumbbell roll toward the stomach.

Name: Glute bridge
Description: A bodyweight hip lift that loads the lower and middle gluteus maximus.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat, about hip width apart.
1. Press the heels down and lift the hips.
2. Squeeze the lower and middle gluteus maximus, and stop when the hips are in line with the knees and shoulders.
3. Lower the hips to the floor with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Pushing the ribs up into a deep arch, or letting the knees fall outward without control.

Name: Glute drive
Description: A machine hip thrust that loads the lower and middle gluteus maximus.
Instructions:
Setup: Set the back pad and the hip pad so the knees are bent and the feet are flat when you sit in the machine.
1. Drive the hips forward until they are extended.
2. Squeeze the lower and middle gluteus maximus, and keep the ribs down and the chin slightly tucked.
3. Return with control without losing contact with the back pad.
Breathing: Exhale as you drive. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Overarching the lower back or pushing only through the toes.

Name: Cable glute kickback
Description: A cable kick that loads the upper gluteus maximus while the gluteus medius keeps the hip square.
Instructions:
Setup: Attach an ankle cuff to a low cable. Stand tall and hold the machine for balance.
1. Sweep the working leg back a comfortable distance without swinging the torso.
2. Squeeze the upper gluteus maximus and keep the hips square.
3. Return the leg with control.
Breathing: Exhale as the leg moves back. Inhale as it returns.
Common mistakes: Arching the lower back or turning the movement into a big kick with momentum.

Name: Standing dumbbell calf raise
Description: A standing heel raise with a dumbbell for the calves.
Instructions:
Setup: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and use the other hand for balance. Stand with the balls of the feet on a step if you have one, or flat on the floor.
1. Rise onto the balls of the feet.
2. Pause briefly at the top without bouncing.
3. Lower the heels slowly, dropping them slightly below the step if you are using one.
Breathing: Exhale as you rise. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom or bending the knees to help the heels rise.

Name: Bodyweight calf raise
Description: A standing heel raise using body weight.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand near a wall or chair for balance, with the feet hip width apart.
1. Rise onto the balls of the feet.
2. Hold the top for a moment.
3. Lower the heels all the way down.
Breathing: Exhale as you rise. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Rushing the reps or bending the knees so the thighs do the work.

Name: Standing calf raise machine
Description: A standing machine heel raise for the calves.
Instructions:
Setup: Set the shoulder pads and place the balls of the feet on the platform.
1. Drop the heels to a comfortable stretch.
2. Rise onto the balls of the feet.
3. Lower with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you rise. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Bouncing into a painful stretch or bending the knees to move the weight.

Name: Seated calf raise machine
Description: A seated machine heel raise for the calves.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit with the pads on the lower thighs and the balls of the feet on the platform.
1. Lower the heels.
2. Press through the balls of the feet to lift the heels.
3. Lower again without bouncing.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the thighs off the pad or using a range that feels sharp in the ankle.

Name: Weighted crunch
Description: A short-range crunch with a light dumbbell held at the chest.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on your back with the knees bent and a light dumbbell held at the chest.
1. Curl the ribs toward the pelvis a short distance.
2. Keep the lower back from yanking off the floor.
3. Lower the shoulders with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl up. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Pulling on the neck, or turning the crunch into a full sit-up by swinging the arms.

Name: Plank
Description: A bodyweight hold that keeps the trunk steady.
Instructions:
Setup: Rest on the forearms and toes, with the elbows under the shoulders.
1. Set the body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Gently brace the abdomen and squeeze the glutes.
3. Hold while breathing, then rest the knees down when the position starts to sag.
Breathing: Breathe steadily. Do not hold the breath for the whole set.
Common mistakes: Letting the hips sag, hiking the hips up, or shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.

Name: Abdominal crunch machine
Description: A seated machine crunch for the abdominals.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit with the chest pad or handles at the upper chest and the feet secured if the machine has restraints.
1. Curl the ribs toward the pelvis.
2. Keep the movement smooth and short.
3. Return to the start without letting the stack slam.
Breathing: Exhale as you crunch. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Pulling with the arms or bending only at the hips while the trunk stays rigid.

Name: Cable crunch
Description: A kneeling cable crunch for the abdominals.
Instructions:
Setup: Kneel facing a high cable and hold the rope beside the head.
1. Curl the ribs toward the pelvis while the hips stay relatively still.
2. Keep the rope beside the head rather than pulling it with the arms.
3. Return to a tall kneeling position with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you crunch. Inhale as you rise.
Common mistakes: Sitting the hips back onto the heels, or yanking the rope with the biceps.

Name: Dumbbell wrist curl
Description: A small-range curl for the forearms.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit and rest the forearm on the thigh, palm up, with the wrist just beyond the knee. Hold a light dumbbell.
1. Let the wrist extend so the dumbbell lowers.
2. Curl the wrist upward.
3. Lower again without opening the hand.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Using a heavy dumbbell that forces the elbow to bend, or bouncing the weight at the bottom.

Name: Incline dumbbell press
Description: A dumbbell press on an incline bench for the upper chest.
Instructions:
Setup: Set a bench to a modest incline and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand and the feet on the floor.
1. Start with the dumbbells beside the upper chest.
2. Press the weights up and slightly together until the arms are extended.
3. Lower them back beside the upper chest with control.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Setting the bench nearly upright so the shoulders take over, or bouncing the weights off the chest.

Name: Feet-elevated push-up
Description: A push-up with the feet raised so more of the work sits on the upper chest.
Instructions:
Setup: Place the feet on a sturdy step or bench and the hands on the floor slightly wider than the shoulders.
1. Set the body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Bend the elbows and lower the chest toward the floor.
3. Press back up until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Letting the hips sag, or placing the feet so high that the shoulders do most of the work.

Name: Decline dumbbell press
Description: A dumbbell press with the head lower than the hips for the lower chest.
Instructions:
Setup: Secure the feet on a decline bench and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand.
1. Start with the dumbbells beside the lower chest.
2. Press the weights up until the arms are extended.
3. Lower them beside the lower chest with control.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Using a steep decline that strains the head, or letting the dumbbells drift toward the face.

Name: Decline push-up
Description: A push-up with the hands raised so the lower chest does more of the work.
Instructions:
Setup: Place the hands on a sturdy step or bench and step the feet back so the body is straight.
1. Keep the hands under the shoulders.
2. Bend the elbows and lower the chest toward the step.
3. Press back up until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Letting the hips pike up, or using a step so low that the movement becomes a flat push-up.

Name: Dumbbell pullover
Description: A dumbbell arc that reaches the arms overhead and trains the lats.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie across or along a bench and hold one dumbbell with both hands above the chest. Keep a small bend in the elbows.
1. Lower the dumbbell in an arc behind the head until you feel a stretch through the lats.
2. Keep the ribs down rather than flaring the lower back.
3. Pull the dumbbell back over the chest.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you pull the weight back.
Common mistakes: Bending the elbows into a triceps extension, or dropping the dumbbell too far behind the bench.

Name: Dumbbell shrug
Description: A shrug that lifts the shoulders toward the ears for the upper back.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and the arms hanging at the sides.
1. Lift the shoulders straight up toward the ears.
2. Pause briefly at the top.
3. Lower the shoulders back down with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Rolling the shoulders in a circle, or bending the elbows to turn the shrug into a row.

Name: Cable face pull
Description: A high-cable pull toward the face for the upper back.
Instructions:
Setup: Set a cable at face height with a rope and stand facing it, arms extended.
1. Pull the rope toward the face and separate the hands.
2. Finish with the elbows out to the sides and the hands beside the ears.
3. Return the rope until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you pull. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Using the lower back to lean away from the cable, or pulling the rope down to the chest.

Name: Back extension
Description: A bodyweight hinge that lifts the trunk for the lower back.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie face down with the hands beside the head, or stand and hinge the hips until the trunk is near horizontal and the hands rest on the thighs.
1. Brace the abdomen and keep the neck in line with the spine.
2. Lift the chest until the body is straight. Do not crank past a straight line.
3. Lower back to the start with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Throwing the head back, or lifting so high that the lower back pinches.

Name: Concentration curl
Description: A seated curl that isolates the short head of the biceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit and brace the working arm against the inner thigh, palm facing up, with a dumbbell in the hand.
1. Curl the dumbbell toward the shoulder while the upper arm stays against the thigh.
2. Pause briefly at the top.
3. Lower the dumbbell until the elbow is extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the shoulder forward, or lifting the elbow off the thigh to start the curl.

Name: Incline curl
Description: A curl on an incline bench that trains the long head of the biceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit on an incline bench with the arms hanging behind the body and a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward.
1. Keep the upper arms still.
2. Curl the dumbbells toward the shoulders.
3. Lower them until the elbows are extended again.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Sitting up off the bench, or swinging the dumbbells from the shoulders.

Name: Dumbbell kickback
Description: A bent-over extension that trains the lateral head of the triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Hinge at the hips and hold a dumbbell with the upper arm beside the ribs and the elbow bent.
1. Keep the upper arm still.
2. Straighten the elbow until the forearm points back.
3. Bend the elbow to return the dumbbell.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Swinging the upper arm, or using a weight so heavy the shoulder lifts.

Name: Diamond push-up
Description: A narrow push-up that trains the medial head of the triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Place the hands close together under the chest so the thumbs and index fingers form a diamond. Step the feet back.
1. Keep the body in a straight line and the elbows close to the sides.
2. Lower the chest toward the hands.
3. Press back up until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Flaring the elbows, or dropping the hips as the arms fatigue.

Name: Reverse wrist curl
Description: A palm-down wrist curl for the forearm extensors.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit and rest the forearm on the thigh, palm down, with the wrist just beyond the knee. Hold a light dumbbell.
1. Let the wrist flex so the dumbbell lowers.
2. Lift the back of the hand toward the ceiling.
3. Lower again without opening the hand.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Using a heavy dumbbell that forces the elbow to bend, or flicking the wrist at the top.

Name: Heel slide
Description: A bodyweight curl that bends the knee for the hamstrings.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on the back with the knees bent and the heels on a smooth floor, or with a towel under the heels.
1. Lift the hips a little and keep them steady.
2. Slide one heel away until the knee is nearly straight.
3. Slide the heel back in by bending the knee.
Breathing: Exhale as you slide the heel in. Inhale as you slide it out.
Common mistakes: Dropping the hips, or sliding so far that the lower back lifts off the floor.

Name: Seated dumbbell calf raise
Description: A seated raise that trains the soleus with the knee bent.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit on a bench with the knees bent and the balls of the feet on a low step. Rest a dumbbell on each thigh just above the knee.
1. Lower the heels below the step.
2. Press the balls of the feet down and lift the heels.
3. Lower the heels again with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom, or letting the dumbbells sit so far forward that the knees take the load.

Name: Reverse fly
Description: A bent-over fly that trains the rear of the shoulders.
Instructions:
Setup: Hinge at the hips with a light dumbbell in each hand and the arms hanging under the shoulders.
1. Keep a small bend in the elbows.
2. Raise the arms out to the sides until they are about level with the back.
3. Lower the dumbbells with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you raise. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Standing upright and shrugging, or swinging the dumbbells with the lower back.

Name: Side plank
Description: A side hold that trains the obliques.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on one side and set the forearm under the shoulder, with the feet stacked or the bottom knee on the floor.
1. Lift the hips so the body makes a straight line.
2. Keep the shoulders and hips stacked.
3. Hold while breathing, then lower and switch sides.
Breathing: Breathe steadily through the hold.
Common mistakes: Letting the hips drop, or rolling the chest toward the floor.

Name: Dumbbell floor press
Description: A floor press for the middle chest that stops the elbows on the ground.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on the floor with the knees bent and a dumbbell in each hand beside the chest.
1. Press the dumbbells up until the arms are extended.
2. Lower them until the upper arms rest lightly on the floor.
3. Press up again without bouncing the elbows off the floor.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Flaring the elbows, or lifting the hips to start the press.

Name: Incline machine press
Description: A chest-press machine set on an incline for the upper chest.
Instructions:
Setup: Set the seat so the handles start near the upper chest and the back pad is slightly reclined.
1. Grip the handles with the feet on the floor.
2. Press until the arms are extended without locking hard.
3. Return until the upper chest is loaded again.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Shrugging, or setting the seat so the shoulders do the whole press.

Name: Decline machine press
Description: A chest-press machine set lower for the lower chest.
Instructions:
Setup: Set the seat higher so the handles travel toward the lower chest.
1. Sit tall with the feet on the floor.
2. Press the handles away until the arms are extended.
3. Return with control until the chest is loaded.
Breathing: Inhale as you return. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom, or letting the lower back arch off the pad.

Name: Floor fly
Description: A bodyweight fly on the floor for the pecs.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie face up with the knees bent and the arms open on the floor, palms up.
1. Keep a soft bend in the elbows.
2. Sweep the arms together over the chest as if hugging a barrel.
3. Open the arms back to the floor with control.
Breathing: Exhale as the arms come together. Inhale as they open.
Common mistakes: Bending the elbows into a press, or jerking the shoulders off the floor.

Name: Bodyweight pullover
Description: A lying arm sweep that trains the lats without a weight.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie face up with the knees bent and the arms extended toward the ceiling.
1. Keep a small bend in the elbows and the ribs down.
2. Lower the arms overhead until they approach the floor.
3. Pull the arms back over the chest using the lats.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower the arms. Exhale as you pull them back.
Common mistakes: Arching the lower back, or bending the elbows into a curl.

Name: Prone row
Description: A face-down row that squeezes the mid-back without equipment.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie face down with the arms hanging or the hands beside the shoulders.
1. Lift the chest slightly and keep the neck in line.
2. Pull the elbows back and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
3. Lower the arms with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you pull. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Yanking the head up, or shrugging instead of pulling the elbows back.

Name: Prone shrug
Description: A face-down shrug for the upper back.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie face down with the arms by the sides and the forehead supported.
1. Keep the neck still.
2. Draw the shoulders toward the ears, then slightly back.
3. Lower the shoulders again.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the whole chest into a back extension, or rolling the shoulders in a circle.

Name: Dumbbell back extension
Description: A hinged lift of the trunk with a light dumbbell for the lower back.
Instructions:
Setup: Hold a light dumbbell against the chest and hinge until the trunk is near horizontal, with the knees softly bent.
1. Keep the neck in line with the spine.
2. Lift the chest until the body is straight. Do not crank past a straight line.
3. Lower back to the hinge with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Rounding the back under the dumbbell, or throwing the head back.

Name: Cable back extension
Description: A cable hinge that lifts the trunk for the lower back.
Instructions:
Setup: Face away from a low cable, hold the handle at the chest, and hinge until the trunk is near horizontal.
1. Brace the abdomen and keep the spine long.
2. Stand tall until the body is straight.
3. Hinge back with control without rounding.
Breathing: Exhale as you stand. Inhale as you hinge.
Common mistakes: Pulling with the arms, or leaning so far that the lower back pinches.

Name: Wall press
Description: A standing press against a wall for the front of the shoulders.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand facing a wall with the hands at shoulder height and the feet a short step back.
1. Lean in until the elbows bend.
2. Press the body away until the arms are extended.
3. Keep the body in a straight line.
Breathing: Inhale as you lean in. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Shrugging, or letting the hips sag.

Name: Bodyweight lateral raise
Description: An arm raise out to the sides for the side of the shoulders.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand tall with the arms at the sides and a tiny bend in the elbows.
1. Raise the arms out to the sides until they are about shoulder height.
2. Keep the shoulders down.
3. Lower the arms with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you raise. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the arms, or shrugging to finish the raise.

Name: Cable reverse fly
Description: A cable fly that opens the arms for the rear of the shoulders.
Instructions:
Setup: Set two cables at shoulder height, cross the hands, and stand with the arms reaching forward.
1. Keep a soft bend in the elbows.
2. Open the arms out to the sides until they are in line with the body.
3. Return until the hands meet in front.
Breathing: Exhale as you open. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Leaning back to swing the cables, or shrugging the shoulders up.

Name: Prone reverse fly
Description: A face-down arm open for the rear of the shoulders.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie face down with the arms hanging toward the floor and a soft bend in the elbows.
1. Keep the neck in line.
2. Raise the arms out to the sides until they are about level with the back.
3. Lower them with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you raise. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the chest into a back extension, or shrugging.

Name: Bodyweight curl
Description: A curl that presses the hands up the thighs for the biceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit or stand and place the heels of the hands under the thighs, palms up.
1. Keep the upper arms still.
2. Curl the hands upward by pressing into the thighs.
3. Lower until the elbows are extended again.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the trunk, or lifting the shoulders to start the curl.

Name: Machine concentration curl
Description: A biceps machine curl with the arm braced for the short head.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit at the biceps machine and brace the working arm on the pad, with the elbow fixed.
1. Curl one arm toward the shoulder while the upper arm stays on the pad.
2. Pause briefly.
3. Lower until the elbow is extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the pad, or leaning back to finish the curl.

Name: Bodyweight concentration curl
Description: A braced curl that presses one hand up the thigh for the short head.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit and brace the working elbow against the inner thigh, palm up.
1. Press the heel of the hand into the thigh.
2. Curl the forearm toward the shoulder while the elbow stays put.
3. Lower until the elbow is extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the shoulder, or lifting the elbow off the thigh.

Name: Cable incline curl
Description: A low-cable curl with the arm behind the body for the long head.
Instructions:
Setup: Face away from a low cable and let the arm hang slightly behind the body, palm forward.
1. Keep the upper arm still.
2. Curl the handle toward the shoulder.
3. Lower it until the elbow is extended again.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the cable, or letting the elbow drift forward.

Name: Bodyweight incline curl
Description: A curl with the arm behind the body for the long head.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit tall and reach the working arm slightly behind the hip, palm forward.
1. Keep the upper arm behind the body.
2. Curl the forearm up while pressing the hand against the other hand or the hip for resistance.
3. Lower until the elbow is extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Rolling the shoulder forward, or bending the wrist to fake the curl.

Name: Cable hammer curl
Description: A neutral-grip cable curl for the brachialis.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand at a low cable with the palms facing each other and the elbows at the sides.
1. Curl the handles toward the shoulders without turning the palms up.
2. Keep the elbows still.
3. Lower until the arms are extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the trunk, or turning the movement into a standard curl.

Name: Bodyweight hammer curl
Description: A neutral-grip curl against the thighs for the brachialis.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand with the palms facing the thighs and the thumbs up.
1. Press the fists into the thighs.
2. Curl the forearms up without turning the palms up.
3. Lower until the elbows are extended.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the shoulders, or rotating the palms up.

Name: Bodyweight overhead extension
Description: An overhead elbow bend for the long head of the triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Reach one arm overhead and hold the elbow with the other hand.
1. Keep the upper arm beside the ear.
2. Bend and straighten the elbow, pressing the working hand into the other hand for resistance.
3. Move only at the elbow.
Breathing: Exhale as you straighten. Inhale as you bend.
Common mistakes: Flaring the elbow, or arching the lower back.

Name: Machine overhead extension
Description: A triceps machine used overhead for the long head.
Instructions:
Setup: Set the seat so the upper arms start beside the ears and the hands hold the handles overhead.
1. Keep the back supported and the ribs down.
2. Straighten the elbows.
3. Bend them again without letting the stack slam.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide, or arching away from the pad.

Name: Bodyweight kickback
Description: A bent-over arm extension for the lateral head of the triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Hinge at the hips and hold the upper arm beside the ribs with the elbow bent.
1. Keep the upper arm still.
2. Straighten the elbow until the forearm points back, pressing the other hand against it for resistance.
3. Bend the elbow to return.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Swinging the upper arm, or standing up to finish the rep.

Name: Machine close-grip press
Description: A narrow chest-press machine movement for the medial head of the triceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit at the chest press and take a narrow grip with the elbows close to the sides.
1. Press the handles away until the arms are extended.
2. Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
3. Return until the elbows are bent again.
Breathing: Inhale as you return. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Flaring the elbows, or bouncing at the bottom.

Name: Bodyweight wrist curl
Description: A palm-up wrist curl for the forearm flexors.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit and rest the forearm on the thigh, palm up, with the other hand pressing lightly on the working hand.
1. Let the wrist extend.
2. Curl the wrist up against the other hand.
3. Lower again without opening the hand.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Bending the elbow to help, or flicking the wrist.

Name: Cable wrist curl
Description: A palm-up cable curl for the forearm flexors.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit facing a low cable, rest the forearm on the thigh, and hold the handle palm up.
1. Let the wrist extend so the handle lowers.
2. Curl the wrist upward.
3. Lower again without bending the elbow.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the forearm off the thigh, or using a load that pulls the shoulder forward.

Name: Bodyweight reverse wrist curl
Description: A palm-down wrist lift for the forearm extensors.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit and rest the forearm on the thigh, palm down, with the other hand pressing lightly on the back of the hand.
1. Let the wrist flex.
2. Lift the back of the hand against the other hand.
3. Lower again with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Bending the elbow, or flicking the wrist at the top.

Name: Cable reverse wrist curl
Description: A palm-down cable lift for the forearm extensors.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit facing a low cable, rest the forearm on the thigh, and hold the handle palm down.
1. Let the wrist flex so the handle lowers.
2. Lift the back of the hand toward the ceiling.
3. Lower again without bending the elbow.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the forearm off the thigh, or yanking the cable with the shoulder.

Name: Bodyweight split squat
Description: A split stance squat for one quadriceps at a time.
Instructions:
Setup: Step one foot back and stand tall, with the front foot flat.
1. Lower until the back knee moves toward the floor.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
3. Press through the front foot to stand.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you stand.
Common mistakes: Letting the front knee collapse inward, or leaning the trunk far forward.

Name: Single-leg press
Description: A one-leg press on the leg press machine.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit in the leg press with one foot on the platform and the other foot on the floor.
1. Lower the platform until the knee bends with the heel still down.
2. Press through the whole foot until the knee is nearly straight.
3. Keep the hips in the seat.
Breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you press.
Common mistakes: Locking the knee hard, or letting the knee cave inward.

Name: Seated dumbbell knee extension
Description: A seated knee straightening with a light dumbbell for the quadriceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit tall and rest a light dumbbell on one ankle, with the knee bent.
1. Straighten the knee until the leg is level.
2. Pause briefly without snapping the knee backward.
3. Lower the foot with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the dumbbell, or leaning back to lift the leg.

Name: Bodyweight knee extension
Description: A seated knee straightening for the quadriceps.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit tall on a chair with one knee bent and the foot off the floor.
1. Straighten the knee until the leg is level.
2. Pause briefly.
3. Lower the foot without dropping it.
Breathing: Exhale as you extend. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Swinging the leg, or leaning back to help the lift.

Name: Bodyweight hip hinge
Description: A hands-on-thighs hinge for the hamstrings.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand with the knees softly bent and the hands on the thighs.
1. Push the hips back and slide the hands down the thighs.
2. Stop when the hamstrings stretch and the back is still long.
3. Drive the hips forward to stand tall.
Breathing: Inhale as you hinge. Exhale as you stand.
Common mistakes: Rounding the back, or squatting the hips straight down.

Name: Cable pull-through
Description: A low-cable hinge that drives the hips forward for the hamstrings.
Instructions:
Setup: Face away from a low cable and hold the handle between the legs.
1. Push the hips back until the hamstrings stretch.
2. Keep the back long.
3. Drive the hips forward to stand tall.
Breathing: Inhale as you hinge. Exhale as you stand.
Common mistakes: Squatting the weight, or pulling with the arms instead of the hips.

Name: Dumbbell leg curl
Description: A lying curl with a dumbbell between the feet for the hamstrings.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie face down and hold a light dumbbell between the feet, with the knees just off the edge of a bench or the floor.
1. Keep the hips down.
2. Bend the knees and curl the dumbbell toward the seat.
3. Lower until the knees are nearly straight.
Breathing: Exhale as you curl. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Lifting the hips, or dropping the dumbbell at the bottom.

Name: Dumbbell glute kickback
Description: A bent-over kick that loads the upper gluteus maximus while the gluteus medius keeps the hip square.
Instructions:
Setup: Hinge and support one hand on a bench. Hold a light dumbbell in the crook of the working knee.
1. Keep the hips square so the gluteus medius stays steady.
2. Kick the heel back and up and squeeze the upper gluteus maximus.
3. Return the knee under the hip with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you kick. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Arching the lower back, or swinging the leg.

Name: Bodyweight glute kickback
Description: A hands-and-knees kick that loads the upper gluteus maximus while the gluteus medius keeps the hip square.
Instructions:
Setup: Start on the hands and knees with the hips square.
1. Keep the working knee bent and the hips square.
2. Lift the heel toward the ceiling and squeeze the upper gluteus maximus.
3. Lower the knee without rocking the trunk.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Arching the lower back, or rotating the hips open.

Name: Seated bodyweight calf raise
Description: A seated heel raise for the soleus.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit with the knees bent and the balls of the feet on the floor.
1. Press the balls of the feet down and lift the heels.
2. Pause briefly at the top.
3. Lower the heels again.
Breathing: Exhale as you lift. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom, or lifting the thighs off the seat.

Name: Bodyweight crunch
Description: A floor crunch for the front of the abdomen.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on the back with the knees bent and the hands lightly beside the head.
1. Curl the ribs toward the pelvis.
2. Keep the lower back close to the floor.
3. Lower with control.
Breathing: Exhale as you crunch. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Pulling on the neck, or sitting all the way up.

Name: Dumbbell side bend
Description: A side bend with one dumbbell for the obliques.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand tall and hold a light dumbbell in one hand, with the other hand beside the head.
1. Bend slowly toward the dumbbell.
2. Return to tall, then bend a short way the other way.
3. Keep the hips still.
Breathing: Exhale as you return to tall. Inhale as you bend.
Common mistakes: Leaning forward, or using a dumbbell so heavy the shoulder shrugs.

Name: Cable side bend
Description: A side bend against a low cable for the obliques.
Instructions:
Setup: Stand side-on to a low cable and hold the handle in the near hand.
1. Bend slightly toward the cable.
2. Return to tall and bend a short way away from the cable.
3. Keep the hips still.
Breathing: Exhale as you stand tall. Inhale as you bend.
Common mistakes: Pulling with the arm, or twisting the trunk.

Name: Dumbbell plank
Description: A plank with a light dumbbell resting on the back for the brace.
Instructions:
Setup: Set a light dumbbell across the upper back and rest on the forearms and toes.
1. Make a straight line from head to heels.
2. Brace the abdomen and hold.
3. Lower the knees when the position starts to sag.
Breathing: Breathe steadily through the hold.
Common mistakes: Letting the hips drop, or holding the breath.

Name: Machine brace
Description: A still hold on the abdominal machine that braces the trunk.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit in the abdominal machine with the pad on the chest and a light load.
1. Brace the abdomen as if preparing to crunch.
2. Hold the pad still for a short breath cycle.
3. Release without letting the stack slam.
Breathing: Breathe steadily through the hold.
Common mistakes: Pulling with the arms, or holding the breath until the neck strains.

Name: Paused Dumbbell floor press
Description: A advanced strength version of the Dumbbell floor press.
Instructions:
Setup: Lie on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand, knees bent, and feet flat.
1. Press the dumbbells until the arms are straight.
2. Lower until the upper arms rest lightly on the floor.
3. Keep the wrists above the elbows.
4. Pause for one second at the hardest point. Use one limb only if the trunk stays still.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Bouncing the arms off the floor, or letting the elbows flare straight out.

Name: Full-range Machine chest squeeze
Description: A intermediate muscle growth version of the Machine chest squeeze.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit in the chest press with the handles at mid-chest and the feet flat.
1. Press until the hands are in front of the chest, without locking the elbows.
2. Squeeze the chest for a moment.
3. Return until the upper arms are near the pads.
4. Use the full comfortable range and keep the same speed up and down.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders, or bouncing the stack.

Name: Paused Machine chest squeeze
Description: A advanced muscle growth version of the Machine chest squeeze.
Instructions:
Setup: Sit in the chest press with the handles at mid-chest and the feet flat.
1. Press until the hands are in front of the chest, without locking the elbows.
2. Squeeze the chest for a moment.
3. Return until the upper arms are near the pads.
4. Pause for one second at the hardest point. Use one limb only if the trunk stays still.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you return.
Common mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders, or bouncing the stack.

Name: Full-range Hands-elevated push-up
Description: A intermediate general fitness version of the Hands-elevated push-up.
Instructions:
Setup: Place the hands on a sturdy raised surface, slightly wider than the shoulders, and step the feet back.
1. Bend the elbows and lower the chest toward the surface.
2. Keep a straight line from head to heels.
3. Press back to the start.
4. Use the full comfortable range and keep the same speed up and down.
Breathing: Exhale as you press. Inhale as you lower.
Common mistakes: Letting the hips sag, or shrugging toward the ears.

Name: Paused Hands-elevated push-up
Description: A advanced general fitness version of the Hands-elevated push-up.
Instructions:
Setup: Place the hands on a sturdy raised surface, slightly wider than the shoulders, and step the feet back.
